extracted.intended_audience: users of the Locarno Classification (design applicants, IP examiners, and national/international IP office staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using the Locarno Classification and LOCPUB to determine the correct class/subclass and goods indication for industrial design registrations, including how to read headings, notes, the List of Goods, alphabetical ordering, square-bracketed qualifiers, and the supplementary EPIC tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Locarno Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Locarno Classification consists of a list of classes and subclasses with, as the case may be, explanatory notes, and a list of goods with an indication of the class and subclass in which each good is classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the combination of class/subclass headings, explanatory notes, and the List of Goods together (see Article 1(3) of the Locarno Agreement) when determining classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class Headings indicate general field
rubrics_metrics.description: The Class Headings indicate in a general manner the fields to which the goods in principle belong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use class headings to determine the broad field of the good; do not rely on them alone for specific classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subclass Headings give further specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Subclass Headings give further specification as to the type of goods included in each class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After identifying a class, consult the appropriate subclass heading to refine the classification to the specific type of good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Explanatory Notes and List of Goods to ascertain correct classification
rubrics_metrics.description: For ascertaining the correct classification of a good, the Explanatory Notes relating to the various classes and subclasses, as well as the List of Goods should be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check both the Explanatory Notes and the List of Goods rather than relying solely on headings or one source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and application of Explanatory Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Explanatory Notes can refer to a class or a subclass. The notes of a class apply to all subclasses within that class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting subclass scope, apply class-level notes as well as subclass-level notes; note whether a note explicitly targets the class or a specific subclass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use General Remarks when classification is unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If a good cannot be classified with the aid of the List of Classes and Subclasses, the Explanatory Notes and the List of Goods, the General Remarks set forth the criteria that should be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the General Remarks' criteria as the fallback procedure for ambiguous or difficult-to-classify goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Goods presentation and ID numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The List of Goods is presented in class and subclass order in the 'Classes' tab and in alphabetical order in the 'Alphabetical' tab. Each indication of good has a six-digit identification number (ID No.). Different indications of the same good (synonyms or indications with variant spellings) share the same ID No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the six-digit ID No. to link synonyms/variants and to locate equivalent goods in other language versions of the Classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes-tab formatting and master indication / synonyms
rubrics_metrics.description: In the list presented in class order (Classes tab) the list is in two columns: first column shows the ID No. and the second column shows the indication of the good. When an indication has synonyms and/or spelling variants, the second column contains the master indication on the first line, and the synonyms and/or spelling variants on the following lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the master indication (first line) as the primary term for ordering within the subclass; synonyms/variants follow beneath it (example given: Class 03-01, ID 100325: 'Vanity cases' with 'Toilet cases' as variant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical ordering within subclass (Classes tab)
rubrics_metrics.description: The alphabetical order within the subclass is determined by the first word of the master indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching in class order, alphabetical placement among entries in a subclass follows the first word of each master indication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilingual classes-tab presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the bilingual version (English/French), the list is presented in three columns, the third column containing the French version of the English indication appearing in the second column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the third column to see the authoritative French equivalent; master English indication appears in column two with its French counterpart in column three (example shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical-tab formatting and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: In the List of Goods in alphabetical order (Alphabetical tab) the list is presented in three columns, under each letter of the alphabet; the first column shows the class and subclass, the second column shows the indication of the good, and the third column shows the ID No. The alphabetical order is determined by the first word of each indication, whether master, synonym or spelling variant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the Alphabetical tab, ordering is by the first word of whichever indication (master or variant) is shown under that letter; class/subclass and ID No. are provided alongside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilingual alphabetical-tab presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the bilingual alphabetical version, the list is presented in four columns, the fourth column containing the master indication in French of the English indication(s) appearing in the second column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fourth column to map English indications to their French master equivalents when using the Alphabetical view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Square brackets indicate clarifying/defining text
rubrics_metrics.description: In the List of Goods, an expression between square brackets is in most cases intended to define more precisely the text preceding the brackets, since the said text is ambiguous or too vague for classification purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat bracketed text as a qualifier/definition narrowing or clarifying the preceding term for classification — use it to resolve ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPIC is a supplementary organizational tool (non-official)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Extended Product Indication Classification (EPIC) has been incorporated into LOCPUB and can be consulted when using the 'Classes' tab in view mode 'EPIC' or 'LOC+EPIC'. EPIC organizes goods that share some common characteristics in hierarchical groups within each subclass of the Locarno Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EPIC to assist understanding of which goods belong in each class and to search for adequate terms for design applications; note that EPIC shows hierarchical groups and alternative LOC+EPIC arrangements but is only an auxiliary tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPIC has no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: EPIC is made available in LOCPUB in order to provide the user with an additional tool that can assist him in understanding what type of goods belong in each class and subclass, and in searching for adequate terms to indicate goods in applications for the registration of designs. EPIC does not form part of the official text of the Locarno Classification and therefore has no legal effect in design examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat EPIC groupings as binding for examination decisions; rely on the official Locarno text (classes, subclasses, notes, List of Goods, General Remarks) for legal classification determinations.
